steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Here’s a 60-second, high-level tour of a Transformer:

1. Input Preparation  
 • Token embeddings: turn words (or subwords) into vectors.  
 • Positional encodings: add a signal so the model knows word order.

2. Self-Attention (“What should I pay attention to?”)  
 • For each token, compute three vectors: Query (Q), Key (K), Value (V).  
 • Attention weights = softmax(Q⋅Kᵀ/√d). This tells each word how much to “listen” to every other word.  
 • Multiply weights by V and sum → context-aware representation.

3. Multi-Head Attention  
 • Do several attention calculations in parallel (“heads”) to capture different relationships.  
 • Concatenate and linearly project back to the model’s dimension.

4. Feed-Forward & Residuals  
 • Apply a small MLP to each position independently.  
 • Add residual connections and layer normalization after attention and after the MLP for stability.

5. Stacking Layers  
 • Repeat attention+MLP blocks (e.g., 12–96 times) to build deep representations.

6. (In Decoders) Cross-Attention  
 • Decoder layers attend to encoder outputs so generation can reference input directly.

Because it avoids recurrence and relies on matrix multiplications, it’s highly parallelizable and scales to huge data—driving today’s breakthroughs in translation, summarization, code generation, and more.
